subject: Hosted API commit top-up, staggered SLA windows & invoice timing
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Rivera <sam@crafthouse.media>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API commit top-up, staggered SLA windows & invoice timing

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for the productive call yesterday. Per our conversation, we can support the 35% monthly commit uplift (from 1.2M to 1.62M tokens/day equivalent) starting June 1, with a 30-day staggered SLA window to help you validate traffic patterns across peak hours. Key points I wanted to capture in writing: 

- Commitment: +35% monthly hosted API commit (annualized), effective 2027-06-01.
- Billing cadence: we can pro-rate June for partial month usage, invoice on June 1 for June pro-rated + July full month.
- SLA stagger: high-throughput tier (08:00–20:00 PT) guaranteed 99.5% availability; lower-throughput night tier (20:00–08:00 PT) will have a best-effort fallback with soft-throttle protections during spikes. This avoids immediate heavy capacity reclaims while we ramp.
- Soft-throttle and burst: a 10% burst cushion for two 24-hour windows per month; excess beyond that follows the agreed overage rates.
- Onboarding ops: deployments will use the Dedicated routing policy for the first 60 days, then revert to unified hosted routing unless you elect Dedicated extension.

Can you confirm that procurement can accept a pro-forma invoice and a standard SOW (I attach the high-level SOW draft) and confirm the billing contact? If procurement prefers net-30 vs immediate prepay for the first month we can discuss a one-time ledger hold or a small credit hold.

If that sounds good I’ll route the pro-forma to Procurement and legal for signature and loop Ben on the invoice timing.

Thanks —
Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: SOW_Hosted_Commit_TopUp.xlsx (summary of tiers, effective dates, SLA stagger table)

From: Sam Rivera <sam@crafthouse.media>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Luis Gomez <luis.gomez@crafthouse.media>, Procurement <procurement@crafthouse.media>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 10:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API commit top-up, staggered SLA windows & invoice timing

Thanks, Irene — this looks aligned with what we discussed. A couple quick asks from our side: 

1) Procurement will need a single pro-forma invoice (PDF) and the SOW attached; can you send both to procurement@crafthouse.media?
2) Our CFO, Luis, prefers net-30 whenever possible. If Redwood needs the first month held as prepay, please call that out so we can escalate.
3) On the SLA stagger, we want the ability to flip the high-throughput window by region if our traffic shifts; is that configurable without a contract amendment?

I’m looping Luis and Procurement so they can confirm billing details. If we can get the pro-forma and DocuSign link today, I’ll get procurement moving.

—Sam
Sam Rivera
Head of Product, Crafthouse Media
sam@crafthouse.media
+1 (212) 555-4477

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Hosted API commit top-up, staggered SLA windows & invoice timing

Irene / Monica —

Quick note on the billing options and one small concession we can offer to move this across the line: 

- We can issue the pro-forma and accept a net-30 payment term on recurring months after the first. For the first month (June pro-rate) we typically require payment up-front for new commit uplifts to avoid provisioning churn, but for Crafthouse I recommend a one-time credit hold of $25k against the June pro-rated invoice (applied if they miss payment by 15 days).
- Pricing: rateband follows the schedule in the SOW. If procurement requests a regional high-throughput flip (Sam's question) we can support flips up to twice per quarter without contract amendment; beyond that we'd require a revision.
- Ops: to minimize risk to other customers, set Dedicated routing for the first 45 days instead of 60. That reduces the window on dedicated capacity and eases ops burden.

If you both agree, I’ll prepare the pro-forma (PDF) and the invoice terms and loop Legal if they request changes.

Ben
Ben Carter
Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
+1 (650) 555-0880

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Rivera <sam@crafthouse.media>, Procurement <procurement@crafthouse.media>

Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 12:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API commit top-up, staggered SLA windows & invoice timing

Hi Sam / Procurement —

Thanks — attaching the pro-forma and SOW as requested. Per Ben we agreed to a one-time $25k credit hold (applied after a 15-day payment delinquency on the June pro-rata) and a 45-day Dedicated routing onboarding window. I’ve also included the small table that shows the configurable "high-throughput" flip allowance (up to 2 flips/quarter without amendment).

Next steps: 
- Procurement: confirm billing contact and whether you will sign via DocuSign or provide a PO number to procurement@crafthouse.media.
- We sent DocuSign envelope here: https://www.docusign.com/Envelope/ABC123456789 — signing should take ~2 minutes.
- Ops: Ben / Monica will start scheduling the Dedicated routing slot for 2027-06-01.

If procurement wants net-30 for recurring invoices we can accept that after the first paid month — please note the credit hold above only applies to the first-month uplift.

Best,
Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: ProForma_Invoice_Crafthouse_May2027.pdf, SOW_Hosted_Commit_TopUp.xlsx
